name: Cryptomnesia
description: A person mistakes a forgotten prior exposure for a brand-new idea of their own. Something retrieved from memory is experienced as originality because its source has been lost.
design_relevance_note: Mostly relevant to internal creative work, not end-user interface behavior: design teams can mistake recalled competitor patterns, workshop ideas, or prior copy for fresh ideation, especially in AI-assisted or highly referential workflows.
prevalence_note: Known in memory and creativity research and occasionally in writing/innovation discussions, but not a mainstream named UX or product-design heuristic.

findings.description: In group idea-generation tasks, participants sometimes later claimed another person's earlier idea as their own novel thought while failing to remember its true source, experimentally demonstrating cryptomnesia as inadvertent plagiarism.
findings.source_venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Learning, Memory, and Cognition
